messages.content: Mr. Isaac rides his bicycle at the rate of 10 miles per hour for 30 minutes. If he rides for another 15 miles, rests for 30 minutes, and then covers the remaining distance of 20 miles, what's the total time in minutes took to travel the whole journey?

First, I calculate the distance Mr. Isaac covers in the first 30 minutes. Since he rides at 10 miles per hour, in 30 minutes (which is 0.5 hours), he covers:
\[ 10 \, \text{miles/hour} \times 0.5 \, \text{hours} = 5 \, \text{miles} \]

Next, he rides an additional 15 miles. The time taken for this part is:
\[ \frac{15 \, \text{miles}}{10 \, \text{miles/hour}} = 1.5 \, \text{hours} = 90 \, \text{minutes} \]

After that, he rests for 30 minutes. Then, he covers the remaining 20 miles. The time taken for this part is:
\[ \frac{20 \, \text{miles}}{10 \, \text{miles/hour}} = 2 \, \text{hours} = 120 \, \text{minutes} \]

Now, I sum up all the times:
\[ 30 \, \text{minutes} + 90 \, \text{minutes} + 30 \, \text{minutes} + 120 \, \text{minutes} = 270 \, \text{minutes} \]

FINAL: 270
